title: The Golden Rule, Imperial, Superior and Boys in Blue bands
summary: Barnes names bands of the period and their leaders: Buddy Petit's Boys in Blue, Sugar Johnny's Imperial, and the Golden Rule with swapping personnel.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well, we all put, partly was in the, hooked up with the same band, cause, uh, you see, in them things we had, let's see, you had the Golden Rule, had the Golden Rule, had the Imperial, you had the Superior, you had the Boys in Blue.
Who were the Boys in Blue?

Well, the Boys in Blue, that was Buddy Petit. That's Buddy Petit, well, sometime you'll get Buddy Petit on that, and you had, uh, the Imperial Band, that was, uh, Johnny Smith. That's Sugar Johnny? Sugar Johnny, you understand? And, uh, well, I don't know, it's a good man of Marquette never get together, I believe it'll take me 50 years to get that together. Yeah. Who was in the Golden Rule?
I can't ever keep that band straight.

That Golden Rule, let's see how the Golden Rule, that Golden Rule, Rondine, they were Gilles Duvarny, and, uh, and, uh, those men would swap up, like, you understand, one man quit here to take another man in his place, you know? Like, Gilles, that was a guitar, and T-Bar was a guitar, we, oh, we had some of them that I really hadn't forgot all about, guitars, basses, and... Well, who managed it at Golden Rule? Well, the Golden Rule was managed one time by Ambrose, and, uh, another time it was managed by Gilles Duvarny, you understand, and the band would jump, you know, like, if you got to work and this band didn't have to work, well, you were looking for work, so you'd go to get to work. And who was the leader? The leader of violin always did lead, it was another violin, the violin didn't lead to the clown, they don't have to lead. And those times? And that's the way that we call it, if it wasn't a violin, you had to go to a clown, see, and that's, the way we got it, now it goes to the trumpet. Them times, it's a different, when you come down to an orchestra or string band, like you say a string band, we would call it, that went to a violin or a clarinet.
